start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-it-working so my bakery order page keeps taking orders: request is that orders keep arriving, scope is the page at https://bakery.example.com/order and its order inbox, constraints are no more than 50 checks a day, authorized actions are reading the inbox and restarting the order form."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: its three steps hand back one evidence-backed answer each, kept on the run record.
instructions: 1. Write the request (what must keep working), the scope, the constraints (limits on checks, cost and time) and authorized_actions (what the AI may repair); all four are required.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-it-working" with them. Answer step health first: the outcome contract (what works today, how fresh it must be, what failure looks like) and the resource bounds.
3. Come back to step change only when something meaningful changed (a new event or fresh evidence); the AI does not poll or repeat an unchanged failed attempt.
4. After a repair, answer step restore with proof that the outcome works again, with evidence ids for each claim.
5. Read each answer: unknown state is never reported as healthy; a blocked requirement stays open with its gap.

worked_examples.title: Health of a bakery order page
worked_examples.ask: Run workflow:keep-it-working so my bakery order page keeps taking orders.

input.request: Orders from the order page keep arriving in the order inbox.
input.scope: The page at https://bakery.example.com/order and its order inbox
constraints: No more than 50 checks a day

worked_examples.given: Read from the row of workflow:keep-it-working in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json: the health step asks for the outcome contract, the resource bounds and the capability review. The inbox last received an order 40 minutes ago.
